content: In this review @Yaël Dillies suggested to not use Finset. The main definition is supposed to mirror Submodule.FG, so I wonder whether we should move Submodule.FG from Finset to Set.Finite next. I could look into it, but would first like to know whether there is consensus on this.
IIUC you're asking whether we should make docs#Submodule.fg_def true by definition. I'd be in favour but as long as this lemma exists I don't think it's especially important.

Let me also ask: for mathlib, is there any need or desire to have similar definition be also formally similar (speaking of FG and DualFG), or is this more a "nice to have" and "as long as you can use it easily"? I could implement a dualfg_def as well, or I could build DualFG on Set.Finite. I don't know how to decide this.

Formally similar API is worth having. Sometimes this might come at very high cost: e.g., maybe we have very old API and we've since learned better ways to do things so we don't want to copy it and must therefore choose between costly refactor or a diverging API elsewhere.

In this case if you follow Yaël's advice, which I think you should, it's a very minor point whether to include a lemma analogous to docs#Submodule.fg_def but you might as well (the proof of your version will just be rfl).
